To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
1) The elastic scattering angular distributions and excitation functions for the system 28Si + 28Si could be described very accurately with the use of the microscopic complex potential.
the inelastic cross section for the 28Si + 28Si system is sensitive to the details of the nuclear potential.

the elastic and inelastic cross section data of the 28Si + 28Si system could be described very accurately using fully microscopic complex potentials, and that a phenomenological approach with a reorientation coupling is required for a good fit of the inelastic cross section.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a microscopic complex potential for the 28Si + 28Si system, and a microscopic calculation of the associated matrix element for the reorientation coupling.
the development of a microscopic complex potential description for the elastic and inelastic scattering of heavy ions in the Coulomb barrier region.
the development of an improved microscopic model of nuclear reactions in the intermediate energy region.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
microscopic complex potential calculations are able to describe the elastic scattering data satisfactorily.
the microscopic complex potential description is adequate for the elastic cross sections and the phenomenological calculations for the inelastic cross section.
the microscopic complex potential is able to describe very well the elastic cross sections and angular distributions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the microscopic calculations of the elastic cross sections are quite satisfactory while the inelastic cross section calculations are not satisfactory.

the microscopic potential description is very successful in describing the elastic cross sections, but the inelastic cross section are more sensitive to the small changes in the associated matrix elements.
the microscopic calculations for the elastic angular distributions are very good and the inelastic angular distributions are good but the excitation functions are not.
The main takeaway from our work is that

a microscopic description of the elastic and inelastic cross sections in the Coulomb-nuclear interference region requires a more sophisticated description than the one provided by a purely complex potential approach.
the elastic and inelastic excitation function are very different in nature and hence should be treated independently.
the inelastic cross section data are more sensitive than the elastic data in probing the nuclear potential.
